hypothesis: The sign of ES's past L-session (L = 20 or 40) close-to-close return predicts the sign of the next RTH session's 09:35 -> 15:55 move: trading in its direction with a 1:1 bracket of 0.5 x ATR20 beats side-matched random-timing twins on the same sessions with the same bracket.
mechanism: Underreaction / slow diffusion and hedging-pressure persistence in index futures at 1-12 month lookbacks; the 1:1 ATR bracket is itself vol scaling in R terms only (the USD max-year-share gate is at 1 MES per trade).

sources.summary: Moskowitz, Ooi & Pedersen (2012, JFE 104(2) 228-250): TSMOM returns positive for every one of the 58 instruments (equity index, bond, FX, commodity futures); significant at the asset-class and portfolio level; persistence over 1-12 months, partial reversal later. Monthly lookbacks and holding, not daily.

sources.primary: Kim, Tse & Wald (2016), 'Time series momentum and volatility scaling', Journal of Financial Markets 30, 103-124
sources.summary: SECONDARY, UNVERIFIED against the primary paper: per the Quantpedia summary of Kim, Tse & Wald (2016, JFM 30, 103-124), much of TSMOM alpha comes from vol scaling (1.27% -> 0.41%/month without), and the unscaled edge vanishes post-crisis 2009-2013, inside our dev window.

prior: Weak. TSMOM's documented payoff is monthly holding over 1-12 months; a one-session RTH hold captures 1/20-1/40 of a monthly hold and misses the overnight, so even the paper's full effect would be ~0.01-0.03R per trade here. Kim-Tse-Wald (secondary summary) find the unscaled edge gone 2009-13. Power: with ~1,950 trades, twin p < 0.005 needs ~+0.05-0.06R over the twins (twin sd ~0.019 at n ~1,985, from the sanity run). The binding gates are the CI low > 0 (net >~ +0.04R) and stress > 0 (gross >~ 0.14R, since stress about doubles the 0.069R cost). Side-matched twins (twins.py: a side-matched permutation over the same sessions): with long share ~0.68 (L20) / ~0.74 (L40) in dev the twins carry the same long share, so the test is timing (does the trend sign pick the better days?), not the S&P's long drift. Expect FAIL.

timestamp_semantics: bar['hist'] holds only sessions strictly before today (frozen eval, tests); 'ret' is the same-contract close-to-close return, roll-adjusted with the Globex switch gap measured before 09:30. Decision on slot 0's close (09:35); the slot 0 close is used only as the bracket centre.
features: S_L = sum of ret over hist[-L:] (the last L hist entries); needs len(hist) >= L and every ret not None, else no signal. side = +1 if S_L > 0, -1 if S_L < 0, no trade if S_L == 0.

Entries with nyse_skipped > 0 COUNT as recorded: their ret spans the missing Databento sessions (c vs the previous listed close), so S_L still covers the whole price path; the window then spans L listed sessions, more than L NYSE days. Count-only: 59 (L20) / 119 (L40) dev trade sessions have such an entry in their window (2014 gaps).
Half-day sessions in hist count as recorded; only TODAY being a half day skips the trade.

On val1/val2 the loader keeps only 60 calendar days (~41 sessions) before the split: the first hist entry has ret None and L40 may have no signal on the first sessions. Those sessions are 'no signal' and are counted in the run report, as in the dev scan.

rules.bars: 5m RTH bars; decision on slot 0's close (09:35), market fill at the next bar's open (09:35); the engine manages the bracket.
rules.sessions: skip NYSE half days; skip sessions where ATR20(tr) over the last 20 hist entries is not computable (controller rule).
rules.entry: side = sign(S_L), every eligible session. One trade per session at most.
rules.risk: stop = c0 - side * k * ATR20, target = c0 + side * k * ATR20, c0 = slot 0 close, ATR20 = mean of the last 20 hist 'tr', k = 0.5. Controller-enforced.
rules.exit: stop, target, or the engine's flat at the 15:55 open.
